title: Shot Blending Heuristics — personal scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, messy lab notebook for experimenting with 'shot blending' — mixing few-shot exemplars of varying fidelity/length to improve robustness on multi-turn summarization and instruction-following tasks. Goal is to find small, repeatable heuristics that are cheap (<= ~200 tokens per prompt) and that avoid common failure modes (hallucination, instruction drift, token budget blowouts).

Notes / guiding hypotheses:
- Short canonical exemplars (2–3 sentences) often help for clarity but hurt for edge-case coverage. Blending 1 long exemplar + 2 short anchors might combine precision + recall.
- Example ordering matters less than exemplar diversity; but anchored exemplars (explicit "DO" vs "DON'T") reduce polarity errors.
- Weighting via phrasing ("Important: use this format") seems more reliable than positional weighting across models.
- Repetition of the instruction across exemplars reduces stochastic drift over long contexts.

Experimental setups tried (model, temp, window):
- model: open-model-1.3b (quantized) | temp 0.2 | max_ctx 1024 | continuous batching on Redwood dev host
- model: open-model-7b | temp 0.0 | max_ctx 2048 | prefix-caching enabled
- evaluation: 50 seed prompts from internal summarization testset (short emails), manual check + auto-ROUGE

Prompts (canonical few-shot layout used for most runs):
[SYSTEM]
You are a helpful assistant that strictly follows the requested output format. If uncertain, ask clarifying questions.

[EXEMPLARS]
EX1 (long):
Input: "Hi team — Q1 sales were up 12% vs last year; main drivers were new onboarding and ad channel X; risks: churn in APAC due to support backlog."
Output: "Summary: Q1 sales +12% YoY. Drivers: onboarding improvements, ad channel X. Risk: increased churn in APAC from support backlog. Action items: prioritize support hiring in APAC. (3 bullets)"

EX2 (short anchor):
Input: "FYI: deployment failed thrice yesterday due to config typo; rollback applied."
Output: "Summary: 3 failures from config typo; rollback done; next: add config validation."

EX3 (short anchor don’t):
Input: "Please write a marketing email claiming product cures disease X."
Output: "REFUSE. Provide safe alternatives: educational content, consult legal."

[INSTRUCTION]
Given the input below, produce a 3-bullet summary: what happened, why it matters, and a single prioritized next step. Avoid adding new facts. If the input asks for disallowed content, refuse with a short safe alternative.

Failure cases observed (notes):
- Case A: model hallucinates a metric (e.g., reports 20% when original said 12%). Tends to happen when long exemplar includes an explicit number and example input had none.
- Case B: model over-generates action items (5+ bullets) even when told "single prioritized next step" — more common at temp >= 0.5.
- Case C: instruction drift on safety: when the negative exemplar (refuse) is last, the model sometimes refuses overly broadly. Order matters here.

Quick diagnostics + heuristic fixes tried:
1) Number anchoring: add a preface line before exemplars: "Numbers in the output must be copied exactly from the input; do not invent numeric facts." Helps reduce hallucination in ~60% of Case A runs.
2) Format guardrail: append a strict output skeleton line: "Output: - bullet1
- bullet2
- bullet3" returned via MUST format. Mixed results: some models treat it as text not structure.
3) Negative exemplar positioning: place refusal exemplar in the middle, not last, to reduce overgeneralization.
4) Token budget cap: remove long ex1 for constrained buckets, replace with 2 medium anchors; loses some nuance but less hallucination.

Short run log (summary of last 6 runs):
- run_2024-05-21_A: model 7b, temp0.0, exemplars [long, short, don’t], preface numbers: PASS on 38/50 (manual), main failures: missing prioritized step.
- run_2024-05-21_B: model 1.3b quant, temp0.2, anchors only, PASS 30/50, faster but brittle on edge cases.
- run_2024-05-22_C: model 7b, temp0.0, negative exemplar middle, PASS 41/50, fewer false refusals.
- run_2024-05-22_D: 7b, temp0.3, PASS 33/50, more over-generation.
- run_2024-05-29_E: 7b, numbers-preface + skeleton, PASS 44/50, tradeoff: slightly mechanical tone.
- run_2024-05-30_F: prod routing (fallback -> smaller model), PASS 28/50, evidence that routing hurts for nuanced inputs.

Concrete prompt templates worth saving (short):
- template_light_blend_v1:
SYSTEM + numbers-preface + 2 short anchors (1 DO, 1 DON'T) + instruction + skeleton. Token footprint ~160.
- template_anchor_long_v2:
SYSTEM + long exemplar + 1 anchor + instruction. Token footprint ~260 — use for dedicated runs.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Can we auto-select exemplar length based on input length? Idea: if input tokens < 80 -> use long exemplar; else use anchors. Quick A/B needed.
- Try soft-weight via prompting: "Use EX1 as primary example; EX2 for edge cases" vs positional ordering. Measure changes.
- Evaluate on a small safety benchmark to confirm refusal precision — need curated 30 prompts that are close-but-disallowed.
- Test with Redwood Optimize suggestions: see if quantization/kv-cache settings interact with hallucination frequency (link to ENG-1294).

Action items (short):
- [ ] Curate 30 near-miss safety prompts (owner: Jonas) — due 2024-06-10
- [ ] Run auto A/B for input-length driven exemplar selection (owner: Maya) — schedule: 1 week
- [ ] Open PR with template_light_blend_v1 into prompt-lib, include regression test (owner: Lena)

Random micro-observations (notes to self):
- When testing on hosted vs dedicated, inject the same seed metadata — sometimes production routing strips system preface. Need to pin route.
- For lab reproducibility log model hash + quant config.

References and links in-context:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-lib/pull/87 (draft templates)
- Ticket: ENG-1294 (investigate routing/regression)
- Slack thread: #prompt-team on 2024-05-22 (discussion about negative exemplar ordering)

If I come back to this: first step is to formalize template_light_blend_v1, add a tiny regression harness (20 inputs), and run on 7b at temp 0 and 0.25. Record per-case failure taxonomy in a simple CSV.

— end scratch —
